_about: v36: how the report's first page ('At a glance') and the fact sheet are built - without AI. The AI story writer (Steps 14-15) starts from the same fact sheet. Validate with: python tools/check_report_blocks.py

headline._drivers: revenue = orders x average order value: the bigger of the two changes is named as the main reason
headline._bands: change of the headline figure in %, from best to worst: strong_up >= 10, up >= 3, down <= -3, strong_down <= -10, otherwise flat

_evidence_parts: parts the story writer may always draw on to explain WHY, even when not ticked (they are added to the fact sheet, not printed unless the writer shows them). Only parts the user may see for this period are used.

facts._importance: figure: weight x |change %| / 10 (points x 2 for rates); finding: severity / rank; action: priority. Higher = more important

personal_data._about: names from these data columns never leave the server: they are replaced by 'Customer A', 'Salesperson B' ... in the fact sheet

analysis._about: v39: root-cause material computed for the analyst (vdash/reports/analysis.py). bridge: which KPIs split the revenue change (orders x basket, items per order x value per item, customers x spend per customer). drivers: revenue breakdowns compared with the comparison period item by item (only complete breakdowns - not top-N lists). sigma: how unusual a day must be to be listed.
analysis._non_additive: breakdowns whose items are averages (not parts of a total): no totals, no share of the total and no share of the total change (also in chart texts, v39.3)
